project_scope.note: First visual module emphasizes the normal leafy family pattern; Cuscuta remains an exception card for later.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look behind the flower: five usually free persistent sepals, then a fused 5-part corolla with conspicuous folds/pleats. Confirm alternate exstipulate leaves and a superior ovary/capsule.
family_diagnostics.habit: Often twining or trailing herbs/vines, but not universally.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Typically alternate, simple and without stipules; shape can vary from heart-shaped to hastate or deeply dissected.
family_diagnostics.flower: Usually radial and 5-merous; corolla fused and commonly funnel/bell-shaped with plicate folds or visible mid-petaline bands.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Common local pattern is a dry capsule with relatively few seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Do not identify a morning-glory from a heart-shaped leaf alone; sepals, corolla folds, capsule and seeds are much stronger.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → diagnostic structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Morning-glories become much easier when you treat the free sepals and folded fused corolla as the family signature, then use leaf/sepal/seed differences for species.

steps.title: 1 · Follow the vine
steps.look_for: Twining/trailing habit with alternate leaves and no stipules.
steps.why_it_matters: This gets you into the right family neighborhood before flowering.

steps.title: 2 · Look behind the corolla
steps.look_for: Five separate or nearly separate persistent sepals.
steps.why_it_matters: The sepals are among the best species-level morning-glory characters.

steps.title: 3 · Read the folds
steps.look_for: A fused funnel/bell corolla with five fold lines or mid-petaline bands.
steps.why_it_matters: Plicate corolla architecture is a strong family cue.

steps.title: 4 · Expect weird leaves
steps.look_for: Deeply divided foliage paired with the same family flower plan.
steps.why_it_matters: Stops the learner from requiring heart-shaped leaves.

steps.title: 5 · Confirm the capsule
steps.look_for: A superior ovary maturing into a dry capsule with a few seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit helps separate Convolvulaceae from milkvines and other twining families.

comparisons.title: Convolvulaceae vs Apocynaceae
comparisons.rule: Morning-glories commonly have alternate leaves, free persistent sepals, plicate fused corolla and capsule. Milkweed-side Apocynaceae has gynostegium/corona/pollinarium machinery and follicles.

comparisons.title: Convolvulaceae vs Passifloraceae
comparisons.rule: Passiflora climbs with axillary tendrils and has corona + elevated reproductive column; morning-glories usually twine by the stem and lack that architecture.

visual_lesson.caveat: Cuscuta/dodders are parasitic leafless Convolvulaceae and intentionally break the normal leafy-vine pattern.
